Subject: AI data use — training opt-out and subprocessors

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we proceed to procurement I need to confirm a few privacy/data-use items so I can clear this with our legal and InfoSec teams. Please see the list below — short answers are fine but we may ask for contract language after that.

1) Training opt-out (no-train): can you commit that Orbital Health customer content will not be used to improve or retrain Redwood models unless we explicitly opt in? If yes, is that a contractual commitment or a technical setting (or both)?

2) Prompt/response ownership: we need language that clarifies Orbital retains ownership of prompts and the model outputs generated from our data — are there any usage rights Redwood requires for model improvement or benchmarking?

3) Subprocessors: please provide your current list of subprocessors (or a link) and your process for notifying us of additions. Any subprocessor that will see customer content must be declared.

4) Cross-border transfers and legal basis: our data residency requirement is US-only for PHI-adjacent workloads. If Redwood routes any requests outside the US, we need to understand safeguards (SCCs, Data Privacy Framework, or hosting options).

5) Evidence: SOC 2 report excerpt (non-redacted) and a point of contact for security questionnaires / audits.

6) Practical implementation: if we opt out of model improvement, what is the developer experience? e.g., API flag, tenant-level toggle, header, or contract-only? Any impact to caching, latency, or access to new feature improvements?

We appreciate concise answers and a short proposed DPA redline you can share.

Best,

Kevin — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers inline below; I'm attaching a proposed DPA with redlines and a SOC2 excerpt for your security team to review. I copied Monica (Customer Success) and Lauren (Legal) to help with any contract language.

1) Training opt-out (no-train): Short answer: yes — we offer a contractual commitment to exclude customer content from model improvement. Technically we support this two ways: a tenant-level account setting (for enterprise accounts) and an API-level request flag (DoNotTrain: true) that prevents content from being included in training pipelines. We will include the clause in the DPA.

2) Prompt/response ownership: We do not claim ownership of customer prompts or model outputs. Our standard DPA will state that customers retain rights to their content; Redwood receives a limited license to process the content for the purpose of providing the service only (and we will exclude it from improvement if the opt-out is set).

3) Subprocessors: See attached subprocessor list (and SOC2 excerpt). We provide 30 days' notice for new subprocessors and an opt-out path for material changes. For regulated customers we also offer Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) so data never leaves customer-controlled networks.

4) Cross-border transfers: For hosted customers we use SCCs for EU transfers and participate in the Data Privacy Framework where applicable. For US-only residency (PHI-adjacent) we recommend Redwood Private (or a Dedicated instance) to ensure all processing remains in US regions; we'll reflect transfer safeguards in the DPA.

5) Evidence: SOC 2 Type II excerpt attached. Security questionnaires can be routed to security@redwood.com; we can sign an NDA to share more detailed evidence if needed.

6) Developer experience: If you select opt-out the developer flow is one of these options: tenant-level toggle (console + API) or per-request header (DoNotTrain: true). The header is honored immediately; the tenant toggle applies account-wide. Opting out does not affect latency materially and we do not charge an extra fee for the opt-out on Hosted accounts. Note: some advanced features that rely on aggregated usage signals (e.g., adaptive quantization suggestions) may not be available if you opt out of telemetry required for those features.

I'll follow up with proposed DPA redlines and the subprocessor list as attachments. Let us know if you want a short call with Lauren to walk the wording.

Cheers,
Ben Carter

Kevin — thanks for the patience. Attached are the DPA redlines and the SOC2 excerpt you requested; key items summarized below to make review easier. If you want to escalate any of this to a short call, Lauren is available and I can arrange a 30-minute sync with your legal team.

Summary of commitments and mechanics (Orbital Health / OPP-4821):

1) No-training / Model improvement opt-out
- Contract: Redwood will include the following clause in the DPA: "Redwood shall not use Customer Content to train, improve, or adapt Redwood's models or model weights, nor include Customer Content in datasets used for model benchmarking, unless Customer provides explicit written opt-in."
- Technical enforcement: DoNotTrain is supported as a per-request header (DoNotTrain: true) and an account-level setting (console/API) that applies to all requests for the tenant.
- Auditability: Redwood will maintain an immutable audit log showing requests marked DoNotTrain and the exclusion actions for 12 months; excerpt samples are available on request.

2) Ownership and usage rights
- Customer retains ownership of prompts and generated outputs. Redwood's license is strictly to provide the service and is limited to processing and ephemeral caching necessary for serving responses. The DPA redlines clarify this language.

3) Subprocessors and notice
- Current subprocessors list is attached. Redwood provides 30 days' notice for new subprocessors. For material changes, we provide an opt-out pathway and will engage on alternatives (including Dedicated or Private deployments).

4) Data transfers and residency
- For cross-border transfers we rely on SCCs for EU transfers and Data Privacy Framework where applicable. For US-only residency and PHI-adjacent workloads we recommend Redwood Private or a Dedicated US-only deployment; we'll reflect residency options in the DPA.

5) Evidence and audits
- Attached: SOC 2 Type II excerpt. Security questionnaires can be routed to security@redwood.com. We can provide further artifacts under an NDA and schedule a SOC walk-through if needed.

6) Developer experience and feature impact
- The opt-out will be honored in real-time with the DoNotTrain header or tenant toggle. There is no additional fee for the opt-out on hosted accounts. Note that certain aggregated, opt-in-only features (adaptive telemetry-driven suggestions) may not be available when telemetry is disabled at the tenant level.
